name: 1730 S. Prairie Avenue — the alley building of the house at 1730 (district draft; refined by T-1932)

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1840 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.

placement.position_note: The rear corner of the main body's rectangle (lot frame u 1.000, v -8.750 m from the middle of the rear lot line), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the sheet's georeference carries no independent check, so its own fit residual, 2.46 m RMS on its control crossings, is all that is claimed. Rotation -0.582 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.
placement.symbolic_location: 1730 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1730 (data/street_grid/1904.json), west side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 16th to 18th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 20).

footprint.note: The main body: the largest rectangle that fits inside the traced main part (u toward the street, v along the front). The building's other rectangles are in draft_plan.

stories.note: The census reading '2-storey and 1-storey brick pieces with a long 1-storey brick range on the alley': 2 storeys.

construction.note: The trace's fabric colour on the main part: brick.

parts.from: s20fp-1730-b2 p2 (main, brick), rectangle 1 of that part; the part's rectangles cover 83% of its fill
s20fp-1730-b2 p1 (range, brick), rectangle 1 of that part; the part's rectangles cover 89% of its fill

draft_plan.note: Rectangles fitted inside the traced parts by the rules' fit (cell 0.25 m, at most 3 a part, to 90% cover): s20fp-1730-b2 p2 (main, brick), rectangle 1 of that part; the part's rectangles cover 83% of its fill; s20fp-1730-b2 p1 (range, brick), rectangle 1 of that part; the part's rectangles cover 89% of its fill. Roles: the main part's largest rectangle is the main body; a shallow rectangle at the front is a bay; the sheet's ranges, porches and stone fronts keep their roles. Storeys per piece and roof per piece are the draft rules' (reconstructed).

draft_elevation.note: RECONSTRUCTED by the draft rules, family row 'service' overlaid with the frontage row: 3B brick, rear 2B, the main block outlined by a dashed line: flat behind a bracketed cornice so that the three brick houses 1726-1736 do not share one roof; which it had is T-1874's. Heights are the rules' starting values inside RECONSTRUCTION-RULES.md's ranges; bays, entrance side, chimneys and dormers are counts the family rules choose, and the seed 1581983062 only tints the fabric inside +-6 %. draft.note: The draft's own provenance: the pass that wrote it, the rows it read and the tickets that replace it attribute by attribute under this id.

function.note: The 1911 sheet reads '2-storey and 1-storey brick pieces with a long 1-storey brick range on the alley'. Backcast to 1904 as a yard outbuilding on the census ruling.

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 20.
what_it_supplies: The Illinois Central / Michigan Central right-of-way and, from the 16th Street row south about 60 m, the water's edge beside it, as of 1911
Footprints, lot lines, street widths (66 ft; 16th Street 50 ft), addresses, material by colour and story counts for Indiana Av. to the tracks, 16th to 18th Street, as of 1911
Its own printed Scale of Feet, which the georeference uses as its scale
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
The lake edge beyond the stretch the sheet actually inks: the pen line stops while the tracks run on

research_note: A DISTRICT DRAFT (T-2334, the owner's district pass of 2026-10-08): a serviceable first model, complete from the street, the walks, the alley and the air, that T-1932 refines in place under this same id. Written by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py from the sheet 20 trace (s20fp-1730-b2), the T-1840 census (s20-1730-r1) and the T-1837 register row frontage-20-020; every height, roof, opening and feature is the draft rules' reconstruction (data/components/prairie_1904/draft_prairie_1904.json; liberty L-draft-prairie-16-18-west-2334).
